prompt: 2.In many countries around the world, rural people are moving to cities, so the population in the countryside is decreasing. Do you think this is a positive or a negative development?
essay:
One of the global issues of the 21st century is urbanization. A growing number of those who live in the countryside are moving to a metropolis every year due to various reasons, such as better job prospects and improved social infrastructure. Consequently, the population density in rural expanse has a tendency to decrease. I firmly believe this constitutes a largely negative development, chiefly due to the risk of the local culture and heritage disappearing and the transformation of rural settlements into ghost towns.

The most troubling consequence of rural population decline is the loss of cultural diversity. Municipality brings together the public from all over the world, each with their own language and traditions. As a result, when rural residents move to urban areas, they often abandon their cultural identity and forget their regional history and native language. For example, in many European hamlets, traditional dances and local dialects have disappeared because the younger generation has moved to cities. This means that unique cultural heritage is lost forever. This affects both generations: young people lose their connection to their roots and feel disconnected from their family history, while older people feel isolated because the traditions they grew up with are no longer practiced.

A further adverse implication is the transformation of rural space into abandoned villages. As more families relocate to downtown, rural regions face a growing shortage of workforce, which threatens local agriculture and businesses. Moreover, social infrastructure, such as hospitals and schools, closes down, and villages turn into ghost towns, where only elderly people remain. For example, in Spain and Italy, many villages have been abandoned because the younger generation has moved to cities. In Japan, more than 800 settlements are at risk of disappearing entirely. This affects elderly residents most severely. Without schools and hospitals nearby, they must travel long distances for basic services, and many feel abandoned and lonely.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that the decline of rural populations is a largely negative development. The loss of cultural identity and the transformation of villages into ghost towns are serious consequences that affect both individuals and society.
